  children={"Register one coded location slot"}
>
</Heading>

<MethodEndpoint
  method={"post"}
  path={"/locations"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



The core operation of this service. Registering a LocationSlot is a chain-of-custody check, not a bare insert: the Site, Zone and Aisle implied by the LocationCode's segments must all resolve to existing, Active aggregates (404 if any link is missing, 409 if one exists but is no longer Active), and the slot's LocationType must satisfy every PlacementRule applicable to its Zone (422, naming the violated rule, if not). There are no orphan slots, ever.

`capacityOverride` is optional; omit it to inherit the LocationType's default envelope. The LocationCode is the slot's identity, so re-registering one already in use is a 409 — including when the existing slot is Decommissioned, since decommission is one-way and a retired code is never resurrected by re-registration. Publishes LocationSlotRegistered.

  as={"h2"}

  parameters={[{"name":"Idempotency-Key","in":"header","required":true,"description":"Caller-generated key (a UUID per logical submit, 1-128 printable ASCII characters) that makes a retried POST safe (ADR 0019, ADR 0044). Clients MUST always send it: the service runs on Postgres in every deployment (ADR 0039), so the header is always enforced and an absent key is answered 400 `idempotency-key-required`, a malformed one 400 `idempotency-key-invalid`. A replay with the same key, method, path and body returns the original response verbatim plus the response header `Idempotency-Replayed: true`; the same key with a different method, path or body is 409 `idempotency-key-reused`. The key is global (not per route).","schema":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":128,"example":"5b0f6a0e-6a41-4c63-9f33-0c8f5c1d2a77"}}]}
